description: How to reproduce PROC SORT (ordering, DESCENDING, NODUPKEY/NODUP, stable ties) with pandas sort_values/drop_duplicates.

proc_sort_to_pandas.title: PROC SORT ... BY ... maps to sort_values, with DESCENDING applying only to the variable it precedes.
rule: `PROC SORT DATA=a OUT=b; BY x descending y;` -> `b = a.sort_values(["x", "y"], ascending=[True, False])`.
SAS default is ascending; `DESCENDING` applies to the variable that follows it, not to every BY variable.
`NODUPKEY` keeps the first row per BY group -> `.drop_duplicates(subset=by_vars, keep="first")` after sorting.
pitfalls: SAS sort is stable within ties only when EQUALS is set; use `kind="mergesort"` in pandas for a stable sort when row order matters for QC.
Applying one DESCENDING to all BY variables inverts the wrong columns -- it only flips the single variable it precedes.
